summary.headline: Zydus Q4 FY26 revenue up 16% YoY to ₹75.9bn with EBITDA margin at 33.7%; FY27 guided to high-teens consolidated growth and >24% margin.
summary.overview: Zydus closed FY26 with consolidated revenue of ₹271.5bn (up 17%) and EBITDA of ₹84.8bn (up 20%), with a record 31.2% full-year EBITDA margin. Q4 revenue of ₹75.9bn rose 16% YoY and 11% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 33.7%, helped by product mix, operating leverage and forex. The company made several acquisitions (Comfort Click, Amplitude Surgical, LiqMeds) and proposed the Assertio Holdings deal for US specialty oncology, while net debt/EBITDA was 0.5x at March 2026. Management guided FY27 to high-teens revenue growth and EBITDA margin above 24%, with US growth in single digits on a high base.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +20% YoY, +41% QoQ; margin +110 bps YoY, +720 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Net profit adjusted for exceptional expense (Q4 FY26)

segments.name: North America (US + Canada)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹29.5 bn, up 5% QoQ, driven by base volume, launches and specialty/rare disease traction. Filed 3 ANDAs, received 9 approvals and launched 6 generics in Q4; launched Zycubo (Menkes disease) via Sentynl, taking its rare disease products to 3.

segments.name: India branded formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 growth 15% YoY, ahead of market; chronic share 46.3% (IQVIA MAT Mar-26), up 620 bps over 3 years. Launched world's first Nivolumab biosimilar (Tishtha) and India's first Aflibercept biosimilar (Anyra), plus semaglutide in a reusable multi-dose pen.

segments.name: International markets formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹8 bn, up 45% YoY, broad-based across emerging markets and Europe. Management says FY26 growth was 40%+ compound.

segments.name: Consumer wellness
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹14.6 bn, up 61% YoY. Skin and hair care up 39.7%, food and nutrition up 9.4%, seasonal brands down 9.8%; international (incl. Comfort Click) like-for-like growth 31.4%.

segments.name: Medical devices
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue ₹3.3 bn, described as in line with expectations. Amplitude Surgical (French orthopaedics) acquired; management says Amplitude is profitable at 20%+ margin and the platform needs 3-4 years to build strong momentum.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at high teens.
North America expected to grow in single digits in FY27 despite the high FY26 base, aided by portfolio.
India branded business expected to outperform the market by 200-400 bps versus IPM.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided above 24%, after Q4 exit margin of about 25-26%; assumes R&D at about 8% of revenue and absorbs Revlimid and Mirabegron competition and Saro launch costs.
Saro commercialisation adds about ₹70 mn of investment in FY27.
FY27 capex about ₹1,500 crore; quarterly depreciation about ₹550 crore (includes capitalised Mirabegron licence fee amortised to September 2027).
Desidustat China launch expected in Q2 FY27; Saroglitazar PBC NDA acceptance awaited before FDA goal date; semaglutide launches with partners continue.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex expected around ₹1,500 crore, reflecting multiple expansion initiatives; quarterly depreciation around ₹550 crore.

Newly acquired US biosimilar manufacturing facility (Zylidac) to be utilised via BOT-BAL supply to Agenus and new partners; management expects at least 3 years before it is well utilised, with BOT-BAL revenue of only about $10-15 mn.
Medical devices: high-end dialyser membrane facility under development in nephrology.
Ahmedabad SEZ oncology injectable facility received EIR after November 2025 pre-approval inspection.
demand_pricing: US base business at about $300-310 mn run-rate; management expects some erosion from Mirabegron competition, with Revlimid contribution minimal.
Semaglutide: Zydus is number 2 in India by share, with Lupin and Torrent co-marketing; management says forecasts were raised above earlier estimates. Partnership/registration planned for 20+ markets.
India oncology is now over ₹800 crore with the company as the largest Indian oncology player; management said pricing generally deflates and volume growth outpaces value growth.
Trade generics described as neutral to Zydus; own trade generics are a small share of the business.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 outlook for growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: High-teens consolidated growth; North America single digit; India 200-400 bps above market; international and consumer both double-digit or better; margin guided above 24%.

qa_highlights.question: Specialty portfolio size and trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Sentynl has 3 approved drugs and has broken even; 505(b)(2) scaling from FY27 with FY28 stronger; Saro commercialisation is in early stages, with specialty expected to be a meaningful driver over 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Assertio acquisition rationale and Rolvedon positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Rolvedon is a long-acting G-CSF, not a biosimilar, with about 4% volume share; it can be given on the same day, unlike pegfilgrastim, which is dosed the next day. Management says the deal is accretive and will say more after closing; no incremental cost build is planned.

qa_highlights.question: R&D spend and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Guided at about 8% of revenue for FY27; FY26 split was about 50% generics/value-added generics and 40%+ NCEs, biologics and vaccines, with a higher tilt to NCEs and biologics.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is comfortable at about 1x net debt/EBITDA on an ongoing basis; bolt-on specialty/505(b)(2) acquisitions to continue; the international business is also a target area.

qa_highlights.question: Weak operating cash flow in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Mirabegron settlement payable, capex, and acquisition-related working capital build.

risks_watch: US erosion of the ~$300-310 mn base as Mirabegron competition grows; Revlimid contribution now minimal.
Saroglitazar PBC NDA acceptance and FDA goal date still pending; MASH Phase 4 recruitment ongoing.
Assertio acquisition pending closure; net debt rising toward about ₹7,000 crore including buyback and deal (per analyst estimate), with operating cash flow weaker in FY26.
Input cost and freight pressure from geopolitical disruption; management said near-term visibility is limited to three to six months.
Medical devices and BOT-BAL facility utilisation take several years to mature.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 and FY27 growth, with specific numbers offered on guidance. More evasive on the Assertio deal terms (pending closure), Saro commercial spend, and near-term supply chain cost impact, where management said visibility was limited.
key_quotes: Even after adjusting for acquisitions, the base business grew in double digits.
On the profitability front, we surpassed our expectations, achieving the highest ever operating profit as well as margins during the year.
So, we are comfortable around one -times net debt to EBITDA right now on an ongoing basis, so we don't see that as major concern.
So it's very difficult to predict the next three months and six months.
